Supporting a New Model Class

Source: R/doc-pm_coef.R
pm_coef.Rd

Kmatrix, predictmeans, contrastmeans and covariatemeans get everything they need from a model through these six generics. Their default methods work for any model class with the usual methods (coef, vcov, terms, df.residual, family), so many classes need no extra code. For a class that lacks one of these, or needs something special, write a method for the corresponding generic only; nothing inside predictmeans needs to change.

Usage

pm_coef(model, ...)
pm_vcov(model, ...)
pm_basis(model, newdata, ...)
pm_data(model, ...)
pm_df(model, L, ...)
pm_linkinv(model, ...)

Arguments

model

A fitted model.

newdata

A data frame of predictor values (the reference grid).

L

A matrix of linear functions of the coefficients, one row per contrast or mean.

...

Further arguments. Kmatrix() passes terms, contrasts and xlev to pm_basis(), and exclude for gam models.

Value

As described in Details.

Details

pm_coef(model)

Named fixed-effect estimates, with NA for aliased coefficients. Default: coef(model); methods for lme, merMod and glmmTMB return the fixed effects.

pm_vcov(model)

Covariance matrix of the non-aliased estimates. Default: vcov(model).

pm_basis(model, newdata, ...)

Design matrix of the fixed effects for newdata, with columns named as in pm_coef(model). Default: model.matrix() of the model's terms (with their stored predvars, so poly(), ns(), scale() etc. use the fitted basis), contrasts and factor levels. The gam method uses the linear predictor matrix of package mgcv.

pm_data(model)

The data used to fit the model, or NULL (the default), in which case they are found from the data argument of the call, getData(), the model frame or the formula environment.

pm_df(model, L)

Denominator degrees of freedom for each row of L, or NULL (the default) to use the model's single residual df: df.residual(model), or Inf (normal-based) when there is none. Kenward-Roger df for lmer and the rules of nlme for lme are built in.

pm_linkinv(model)

Inverse link function used to back-transform the means, or NULL for none. Default: the inverse link of family(model) unless it is the identity.

The model also needs a terms() method for its fixed effects (used to find the variables in the model), and its call (getCall()) or a pm_data() method so that the data can be found.

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

  library(predictmeans)
  # A made-up model class that wraps lm() and has only four methods.
  fit_mymodel <- function(formula, data) {
    structure(list(fit = lm(formula, data), call = match.call()), class = "mymodel")
  }
  coef.mymodel <- function(object, ...) coef(object$fit)
  vcov.mymodel <- function(object, ...) vcov(object$fit)
  terms.mymodel <- function(x, ...) terms(x$fit)
  df.residual.mymodel <- function(object, ...) object$fit$df.residual

  Oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)
  Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
  m <- fit_mymodel(yield ~ Block + nitro*Variety, data = Oats)
  predictmeans(m, "nitro", plot = FALSE)$means
#> Error in x$terms %||% attr(x, "terms") %||% stop("no terms component nor attribute"): no terms component nor attribute

  # Degrees of freedom of its own, e.g. normal-based:
  pm_df.mymodel <- function(model, L, ...) rep(Inf, nrow(L))
  predictmeans(m, "nitro", plot = FALSE)$means
#> Error in x$terms %||% attr(x, "terms") %||% stop("no terms component nor attribute"): no terms component nor attribute
